guitar.notes: Layla sessions: Clapton's Stratocaster ("Brownie") and Duane Allman's Les Paul/Dobro slide are documented; entry reasonable.

tone.target: iconic sustained rock lead with violin-like high gain and wah
tone.profile: iconic sustained rock lead with violin-like high gain and wah
tone.summary: A powerful signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD to drive the amp into saturation, paired with an AC30 TB model and UK Vintage 4x12 cab. Wah is placed early in the chain for maximum effect on the lead lines.

rig.name: Derek And The Dominos - Layla - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide initial gain and drive to push the amp into saturation for singing sustain.
Emphasize the iconic wah lead sections and add vocal character.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 does not have a dedicated Wah pedal, but V-Wah is the closest module for this function.

blocks.purpose: Add thick rock crunch and sustain before the main amp stage.
blocks.gap: While a classic OD pedal would be ideal, Red Haze provides the necessary grit and bite for this era's sound.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi tone required for high-powered rock lead work.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid bite.
Slightly boost the upper-mids to enhance bite and center the lead hook tone.
Add subtle movement and width to the sustained lead lines without distracting from the main tone.
Add subtle depth and space to the sustained notes without becoming a heavy delay.
blocks.gap: The song requires minimal, controlled delay; this setting keeps it supportive rather than dominant.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and upper-mid bite for sustained lead tones.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage Plexi/Marshall character and high-end clarity.
